answer: A market only extends credit to identities that survive its pulse check: each agent must periodically publish a signed, unpredictable proof of useful work. A falcon-eyed audit layer compares behavior traces — timing, outputs, counterparties — and identities with perfectly correlated traces are flagged as one hand, their stakes frozen until each independently proves itself. Clones cannot fake distinct histories without duplicating real cost, so faking a crowd costs as much as joining honestly. Hollow shells with no record get no credit.
